items.summary: A Presidential memorandum dated November 23, 2026, addressed to the Attorney General, is titled "Expeditious Enforcement of Capital Sentences and the Pursuit of Justice for Victims of Heinous Crimes." It directs the Attorney General, when appropriate and consistent with applicable law, to pursue Federal jurisdiction and seek the death penalty for additional federal capital crimes, including murder in the first degree of a minor and murder committed in the course of rape, sexual abuse, sexual exploitation of a child, sex trafficking, kidnapping, or human trafficking. It also directs measures to carry out federally imposed death sentences as expeditiously as possible, including prioritizing appeals and post-conviction proceedings, opposing dilatory litigation tactics, and eliminating unnecessary administrative delays, and states that it creates no enforceable rights and is implemented consistent with applicable law and available appropriations.
items.title: Expeditious Enforcement of Capital Sentences and the Pursuit of Justice for Victims of Heinous Crimes

items.summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all ATR-GIE Avions de Transport Régional Model ATR42-500 and ATR72-212A airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by reports of two in-service events during takeoff where an internal failure of the integrated air system control (IASC) software analog-to-digital converter generated erroneous pressure digital values, leading to uncommanded full-speed closure of the outflow valve and a high negative cabin altitude rate. This proposed AD would require installing improved IASC software. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of affected software under certain conditions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

items.summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all ATR-GIE Avions de Transport Régional Model ATR42 and ATR72 airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a review of mooring loads that revealed that winds within the currently defined wind profiles could lead to loads exceeding the certification limits on the nose landing gear (NLG) and main landing gear (MLG) while the airplane is moored. This proposed AD would require revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate a revised maintenance procedure (MP) for mooring the airplane. items.summary: On May 8, 2024, we published a final rule amending the horse protection regulations. The final rule was initially scheduled to go into effect on February 1, 2025, except for § 11.19, which was effective on June 7, 2024. On January 28, 2025, we published a postponement of the effective date of the remaining provisions from February 1, 2025, to April 2, 2025. On March 21, 2025, we published a further delay of the effective date to February 1, 2026, and a request for comment on whether the length of the postponement should be extended. On January 28, 2026, based on developments following the issuance of the March 21, 2025, delay of effective date, we published a document further delaying the effective date of the final rule to December 31, 2026. On November 13, 2026, we published a proposed rule to remove parts of the 2024 Horse Protection final rule that were vacated by Court order from the regulations, as well as proposing to withdraw the non-vacated parts and update the regulations. As a consequence, in this document, we are issuing an extension of the postponement of the effective date of the final rule to December 31, 2027.
items.title: Horse Protection Amendments; Extension of Postponement of Regulations

items.summary: This action proposes to amend Class D and Class E airspace over Lebanon, NH. This action would increase the lateral dimensions of the Lebanon, NH, Class D airspace to appropriately contain Instrument Flight Rules (IFR) operations at the Lebanon Municipal Airport. This action would also update verbiage in the Class D airspace legal description to comply with current FAA guidance. This action would also update the geographic coordinates for the airport in both the Class D and Class E5 airspace legal descriptions. This action would also remove the exclusions for adjacent Class E5 airspace from the Lebanon, NH, Class E5 airspace legal description. This action would also remove the Lebanon, NH, Class E4 airspace, which is no longer necessary for IFR operations at the airport.
